run1.title: Baseline
run1.lesson: Left to itself, gradient descent finds a slow fade instead of a reset, and a write gate that records time rather than distance. Both work a little at 10 seconds and not at all at 20. The memory was in F, but leaky.

run2.title: Erase penalty times ten
run2.lesson: Charging more for erasing away from food did not push the gate toward food; it shut the gate everywhere. With no erase at all, the tallies filled to the ceiling within a trip and the brain could not home. A scalar gate cannot be penalised into firing on five ticks out of three hundred.

run3.title: Two seconds at food
run3.lesson: Four times more food ticks did not teach the reset either, but it rebalanced the whole trip: a lower write gate, tallies off the ceiling, and, for the first time, a write gate that follows speed (+0.94). First brain to home on 20-second trips. Memory in F by a wide margin: 1.99 with it, 4.75 without.

run4.title: Five trips per episode
run4.lesson: More trips in a row did not make the erase gate fire at food (0.0045 at food, 0.0085 away: it erases LESS at food than elsewhere). The fade simply absorbed the dirty board, and the extra trips only cost score: 2.30 at 20 s against run 3's 1.90. Prediction failed. It did give the first 30-second numbers: 2.37 with F, 5.80 without, on trips it never trained at, so the memory generalises to longer wanders.

run5.title: Erase penalty ×10, warm start
run5.lesson: The penalty did nothing to the erase gate, because at 0.5 times a gate of 0.01 it adds 0.005 to a loss of about 2: a rounding error. Run 2 had died for cold-start reasons, not because the penalty was strong. What run 5 did show is the danger of long training near the ceiling: after a good stretch (best frozen exam 1.41 at iteration 400) it collapsed twice, and the second time it did not recover; the final network is worse than a random walk. Its best checkpoint ties run 4 at 30 s (2.37). Lesson: the optimiser needs a schedule that shrinks its steps late in a run.

run6.title: Stretch to 30 s, with cosine decay
run6.lesson: Trained at 30 seconds for the first time. By iteration 400 its frozen exam at 30 s was 1.77, far under the untrained 2.37, with the memory in F (5.48 without). Then the familiar collapse at 500 (write gate 0.38 to 0.64, loss to 12) and it did not recover by 600, so it was killed. Cosine decay alone was not enough: at iteration 500 of 1,200 the rate was still two thirds of full. Restarted as run 6B from the 1.77 checkpoint at a third of the base rate. Note: this stage was started on run 5's 64-trip frozen exam of 1.41, not on the running-score rule (which no run had met); see the narrative.

run6B.title: Run 6 restarted at a third of the learning rate
run6B.lesson: No collapse in 800 iterations at 30 seconds. Final network: 2.13 at 30 s with F, 5.91 without (22% arrived); 1.85 at 20 s. The lower rate is the fix for the late collapses: from here every warm start trains at 3e-4. The score has plateaued around 2.1 at 30 s, well above the 0.75 floor. Still a fade (0.005 at food, 0.009 away), write~speed +0.53, tallies saturated a third of the time at 30 s: the three things that still separate it from the fly.

run7.title: Erase penalty 20, warm
run7.lesson: Even a real penalty barely moved the gate: away-from-food erase went 0.0081 to 0.0075 in 200 iterations, and at-food erase fell rather than rose. The diagnosis is structural. The erase gate is a sigmoid whose bias sits near -5, where the curve is almost flat: its slope there is about 0.007, so every gradient reaching the gate, penalty or benefit, is multiplied by 0.007 before it can move anything. The gate is not refusing to learn the reset; it cannot hear the signal. Killed at 200; the fix is tested as run 7B.

run7B.title: Erase gate given a voice (bias +2.5)
run7B.lesson: The first run in which the erase gate prefers food. On the 200-trip test it erases 0.027 per tick at food against 0.009 away, a ratio of 3, with peaks of 0.06 at food; every earlier run was at or below 1. The ratio grew through training (1.1 at iteration 200, 1.5 at 700). It is a leaning, not yet a reset: the fly-like target is near 1 at food and near 0 away. The strong starting fade cost score, 2.55 at 30 s against the parent's 2.13, and 800 iterations were not enough to recover it. Prediction partly met: away-from-food erase did fall below 0.01; at-food erase reached 0.027 mean, short of 0.05; score did not recover.

run8.title: Run 7B continued, unchanged
run8.lesson: Continuing the line with nothing changed did not sharpen the food preference. Over 300 iterations the erase ratio on the sample trip sat between 1.3 and 1.6, with peaks at food of 0.07 to 0.10, while the score recovered to about 2.2. The gate can move now, but with this signal it settles on a mild preference for food rather than a clean reset. Killed at 300 to spend the time on a stronger push.

run8B.title: Food stand 4 s with an audible gate
run8B.lesson: Doubling the food ticks did not sharpen the reset: on the 200-trip test the erase ratio is 3.0 (food 0.027, away 0.009), no better than run 7B's 3, with peaks at food of 0.06. The score held rather than improved: 2.28 at 30 s on the standard exam, though its frozen checks on other trips reached 1.76. Prediction failed on the ratio, met on the score holding. Lesson: once the gate can hear, more food ticks are not the missing signal; the preference for food is real but small, and nothing on the warm-start line has pushed it past a ratio of about 3.

run9.title: Cold start, audible gate, penalty 20
run9.lesson: From scratch, the penalty of 20 did what it did in run 2: it drove the erase gate shut within 200 iterations (0.0001 per tick away from food, 0.001 at food), which puts the sigmoid back on its flat part, deaf again, before any memory had formed. No F-versus-no-F gap by iteration 300. Killed under the five-minute rule. Lesson: on a cold start the penalty must be small enough that the gate stays audible while the memory is being built; 20 is a warm-start number.

run9B.title: Cold start, audible gate, penalty 2
run9B.lesson: Killed at 500 by its own prediction: no memory gap formed (F 2.42, no-F 2.42). The gate closed to 0.001 per tick by iteration 200 even at a penalty of 2, because before any memory exists erasing has no benefit and every gradient says erase less. Worse, the strong early fade (0.07 per tick at the start) wiped the tallies during the phase when the memory had to form; run 3, same seed and a deaf gate, had a 0.5 gap by iteration 300. Lesson: an audible erase gate helps a network that already has a memory (run 7B) and hurts one that does not. The reset can only be learned second, after the tally.

run10.title: Second bias shift, the ratchet test
run10.lesson: The ratio did ratchet, once measured properly. On the single training-check trip it looked stuck near 1.8, but on the 200-trip test the erase gate fires 0.075 per tick at food against 0.010 away: a ratio of 7.4, up from 3 in runs 7B and 8B, with peaks of 0.20 on the test trip and 0.2 to 0.3 during training. The gate is learning a spike at food, one tick at a time. It is also the best earned 30-second score of the night: 2.10 on the standard exam, 23% arriving, with frozen checks under 1.5. Prediction met on the ratio (above 5) and on the score; at-food erase 0.075 is above the 0.05 target. Still not a full reset (that would be near 1 at food), but the clearest one yet.

run11.title: Seed 1 replication of run 3
run11.lesson: The 10-second learning replicated from a different random start, and faster: promoted at iteration 619 against run 3's 804, with a frozen gap of 0.9 (1.46 with F, 2.40 without). The transfer to 20 seconds did not: 400 iterations after promotion the gap had not opened, and the driver's stop rule ended the run. The write gate sat near 0.7 with write strength 0.10, the run 1 pattern where the tallies saturate on longer trips. So the compass-and-tally recipe is robust to the seed; how quickly a given seed adapts to longer trips is not. Queued as 11B: the same network continued at 20 s with the gap rule suspended, since run 3 also needed time after its promotion.

run12.title: Third bias shift
run12.lesson: The ratchet held a third time. On the 200-trip test the erase gate fires 0.213 per tick at food against 0.010 away, a ratio of 20, with peaks of 0.50 on the test trip and 0.57 to 0.67 during training. The reset is now a spike that opens more than halfway at food and nowhere else. The score held: 2.21 at 30 s on the standard exam, 24% arriving, against 2.10 for run 10. Prediction met: ratio target 12, at-food target 0.15.

run13.title: Slow-half fast-half world
run13.lesson: Trained on a world where time and distance disagree, then tested on the standard world: 1.98 at 30 s on the final checkpoint and 1.91 at its best, the lowest earned 30-second scores of the night, with 25% arriving. Write-versus-speed on the standard exam is +0.69 (+0.67 at the best checkpoint), up from run 10's +0.67 but short of the 0.9 predicted. The harder training world made a better brain for the easy one: forcing distance-weighting during training improved homing where speed merely drifts. The reset survived the change of world (ratio 7).

run11B.title: Seed 1, continued at 20 s
run11B.lesson: Given 800 more iterations with the gap rule suspended, seed 1 did begin to transfer: the frozen gap opened from zero to about 0.8 and the running score fell from 4.4 to 3.7. But on the 200-trip test at 20 s it scores 3.87 with F against 4.61 without, still worse than the random walk's 3.61, with 26 compass cells and tallies saturated 59% of the time (write strength 0.165, twice seed 0's). Verdict: the recipe's 10-second stage replicates across seeds; its 20-second transfer is much slower for seed 1 and was not complete after 1,200 iterations. The robustness claim is narrowed to: compass cells and a working tally emerge from any seed; how fast the tally adapts to longer trips depends on the seed.

run14.title: Fourth bias shift
run14.lesson: The ratchet keeps working: on the 200-trip test the erase gate fires 0.37 per tick at food against 0.011 away, a ratio of 33, with peaks of 0.78 on the test trip and 0.83 to 0.91 during training. Away from food it has never moved from about 0.01. The score is 2.06 at 30 s, 26% arriving, the best of the ratchet line and within noise of the campaign best. Ratios across the shifts: 3, 7, 20, 33. Prediction partly met: at-food target 0.4, peaks target 0.8.

run15.title: Delta rule, cold start (Peter's proposal)
run15.lesson: Stopped by the gap rule at iteration 800: no memory formed at all. Under the delta rule F writes only what it failed to predict, so F converged on predicting the network's own next activity from its last, and once it did that it stopped writing; the tallies never accumulated steps, and the write strength and A did not move from their starting values after iteration 100 (0.108 and 0.082, flat). Peter's prediction, that delta would keep a wider memory gap and free the erase gate, did not hold in this form. Two honest caveats: this was a cold start with the deaf-gate recipe, and a warm start from a Hebb-trained network, or a delta rule applied only on the columns A selects, might behave differently. As run, the delta rule is a predictor, not a tally.

run16.title: Fifth bias shift
run16.lesson: Five shifts: on the 200-trip test the erase gate averages 0.52 per tick across the food stand and reaches 0.93 at its peak, against 0.010 away from food, a ratio of 53. During training the peaks were 0.95 to 0.98. The reset is now a wipe: the board is cleared at food and untouched elsewhere. Score 2.14 at 30 s, 25% arriving, within noise of runs 10, 12 and 14, so five rounds of the same move took the mean at food from 0.03 to 0.52 and the peak from 0.06 to 1 without costing the memory or the score. Ratios across the shifts: 3, 7, 20, 33, 53.
